mappings.note: Acts of Union, Italy and Germany are three of the four events, so the sequence is a nation-formation chronology (LO-3); Vienna alone is not enough to pull in LO-2
the Vienna settlement's purpose was to restore the conservative order, which is the conservatism strand of LO-2; the item asks which aim was absent, i.e. recall of the settlement's terms
the kneeling figure can only be named by reading the cartoon of Garibaldi pulling the ITALY boot on to Victor Emmanuel; unification content (LO-3) with a genuine image-reading demand (C-1.2)

absolutist, utopian, plebiscite and suffrage are chapter glossary terms spanning government, vision and voting, and no single learning outcome owns them. Cited as recall alone rather than stretching LO-3; the frame has no vocabulary outcome

the key is 'both a and b', so the student needs the July 1830 regime change (LO-2) and Belgium breaking away as a new state (LO-3); neither outcome alone answers it, which is why two content codes are cited here and not elsewhere

the described group is the post-1815 revolutionaries of the secret societies, one of LO-2's movements; the distractors are conservatives and liberals, so the discrimination is between currents, not between states
Silesia 1845 again, the social-distress strand of LO-2; same mapping as item 16 because it is the same fact asked with different distractors

naming Delacroix requires recognising the Massacre at Chios from the supplied canvas; it belongs to the romantic mobilisation of sympathy for Greece (LO-2) rather than to the Greek state itself (LO-3)
four claims about Marianne and Germania as personifications of the nation, the idea-made-visible content of LO-3; no picture is supplied, so the sifting is recall
Sorrieu, Wolfe Tone, Byron and Karpinski are the artists and agitators of the period's movements (LO-2); the item turns on Sorrieu being French, a biographical fact, so C-1.1

the partitions that erased Poland from the map, the precondition of Polish nationalism, so LO-3. Imperfect: the frame has no outcome for nations that did not become states, and LO-3 is written around ones that did

tricolour, transfer of sovereignty and the mission to liberate Europe all identify 1789, the core of LO-1; the distractors are Germany and Greece, so the discrimination is which event, not which consequence
which claim about the 1707 Act is false (Ireland, not Scotland); British state formation, LO-3, recalled

the assembly in the picture is identified from the black-red-gold hangings and the Germania above the dais, so the image carries the answer; the Frankfurt Parliament is the 1848 liberal revolution, LO-2
definition of conservatism as an ism, LO-2 by the same rule that sends liberalism there; the distractors are plebiscite and absolutism, so it is a vocabulary discrimination
Italy and Germany give LO-3 the plurality over the single Napoleonic and single Vienna event; the sequence is still about when states were made
which Vienna measure was not taken; the German confederation of 39 states was left untouched. Conservative restoration content, LO-2, recalled
the 1688 bloodless transfer of power to Parliament as the mechanism of British state formation, LO-3; the options are rival accounts but all four are textbook statements, so retrieval
defines nationalism itself, which LO-3 names as the idea whose evolution is to be traced; the liberal-nationalism definition items go to LO-2 because there the ism, not nationalism, is the object

the sword in the Germania picture means readiness to fight, a value from the memorised attribute key rather than something the image discloses; so C-1.1 and not the C-1.2 given to items where the picture decides the answer
sovereignty passing to the people and a centralised administration with uniform laws are the revolutionary measures of LO-1; no other country is in view, so LO-3 stays out
Clasen is named only by recognising Germania on guard on the Rhine from the supplied painting, the same image-decides-it test as the Huebner item; allegory content is LO-3
two statements about why the Silesian weavers rose, both true; LO-2 again, with the demand still verification of a remembered cause
1814 Vienna and 1848 revolutions give LO-2 the plurality over one Napoleonic and one Greek date; the run is anchored on the age of revolutions rather than on any state being made
which belief conservatives did NOT hold, turning on their acceptance of modernisation; conservatism as an ism is LO-2, and all four options are textbook statements so the demand stays recall
